lesson.text: Quick memory: in grade 6 you met Magna Carta. In which year did King John seal it? (1215.) Today: how kings, queens and Parliament argued over power between 1509 and 1745.

The Tudors ruled England from 1485 to 1603. Henry VIII (ruled 1509-1547) married six times. The Pope would not end his first marriage. So in 1534 Parliament made Henry head of the Church in England, and it broke with Rome.

Henry's three children ruled in turn: Edward VI, Mary I and Elizabeth I, and their different beliefs changed the Church each time. Elizabeth I (1558-1603) never married; her navy beat the Spanish Armada in 1588, and Shakespeare wrote in her time.

Elizabeth had no children. So in 1603 James VI of Scotland became James I of England too: the first Stuart king. He and his son Charles I believed God gave kings the right to rule. They quarrelled with Parliament over taxes and religion.

Charles I ruled without Parliament from 1629 to 1640. In 1642 civil war broke out between Royalists (Cavaliers) and Parliamentarians (Roundheads). Parliament won, and in 1649 Charles was tried and put to death. England became a republic.

Oliver Cromwell led the republic as Lord Protector from 1653 until he died in 1658. In 1660 the monarchy returned with Charles II. In 1688 James II clashed with Parliament and fled. His daughter Mary II and her husband William III took the throne.

In 1689 the Bill of Rights said the monarch needs Parliament to make laws and raise taxes. Elections must be free, and members may speak freely in Parliament. In 1707 England and Scotland united as Great Britain. Parliament now held the real power.

Try it in the world: hold a debate in your world's parliament hall: should a ruler be able to raise taxes without a vote? Write the rule you agree on a sign, like the Bill of Rights. Next: spices, trade and companies.

exercises.prompt: Who became head of the Church in England in 1534?
exercises.hint: He wanted his first marriage ended.
exercises.explain: Henry VIII: Parliament made him head of the Church in England in 1534.

exercises.prompt: Whose navy beat the Spanish Armada in 1588?
exercises.explain: Elizabeth I's navy beat the Spanish Armada in 1588.

exercises.prompt: Charles I believed God gave kings the right to rule.
exercises.hint: This belief is called the divine right of kings.
exercises.explain: True: it is called the divine right of kings.

exercises.prompt: What were Parliament's soldiers in the Civil War called?
exercises.hint: The king's side were the Cavaliers.
exercises.explain: Roundheads; the king's side were the Cavaliers.

exercises.prompt: Which family ruled England from 1485 to 1603?
exercises.hint: Henry VIII and Elizabeth I belonged to it.
exercises.explain: The Tudors, from Henry VII in 1485 to Elizabeth I in 1603.

exercises.prompt: Henry VIII ruled from 1509 to 1547. For how many years?
exercises.hint: Take the first year from the last.

exercises.prompt: Look at the family tree. Which of Henry VIII's children ruled last?
exercises.hint: Compare the years under their names.
exercises.explain: Edward VI ruled 1547-1553, Mary I 1553-1558, Elizabeth I 1558-1603: Elizabeth ruled last.

exercises.prompt: Put these in order, earliest first.
exercises.hint: The smaller the year, the earlier.

exercises.prompt: Match each word to its meaning.
exercises.hint: Two sides of a war, a title and a law.
exercises.explain: Cavaliers: the king's side. Roundheads: Parliament's. Lord Protector: Cromwell. Bill of Rights: limits on the monarch.

exercises.prompt: Sort these monarchs: Tudor or Stuart?
exercises.hint: The Tudors ruled until 1603; the Stuarts from 1603.
exercises.explain: Tudor: Henry VIII, Elizabeth I, Edward VI. Stuart: James I, Charles I, Anne.

exercises.prompt: Why did Parliament and Charles I go to war?
exercises.hint: What did Charles do from 1629 to 1640?
choices: they argued over power, taxes and religion
exercises.explain: Charles ruled and taxed without Parliament and they disagreed over religion: a struggle over who held power.

exercises.prompt: After 1689 a British monarch could raise taxes without Parliament.
exercises.hint: What did the Bill of Rights say about taxes?
exercises.explain: False: the Bill of Rights said taxes need Parliament's agreement.

exercises.prompt: England became a republic in 1649, and the monarchy returned in 1660. How many years without a king or queen?
exercises.hint: Take the first year from the last.

exercises.prompt: What is a constitutional monarchy, as Britain became?
exercises.hint: Think of the Bill of Rights.
choices: a monarch limited by laws and Parliament
a king who makes every law alone
exercises.explain: A monarch reigns, but laws and an elected Parliament limit the monarch's power.

exercises.prompt: Magna Carta was sealed in 1215 and the Bill of Rights passed in 1689. How many years apart?
exercises.hint: Take the earlier year from the later one.
